- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true outcome, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window; reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 3–7% to align with true trend.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model is prone to lagging; add 1–2 days of delay in price response to forecast (i.e., shift forecast 1–2 days ahead).
